cur:catacombs-via-anapo-multiplication.summary: Against a light ground a young, beardless Christ in a long tunic and pallium bends forward and touches with a rod a row of seven baskets of bread at his feet. With a single figure and a row of baskets the painter evokes the feeding of the multitude, a sign of the Eucharist and of the heavenly banquet.
facts: The rod with which Christ touches the baskets is the usual sign of miraculous power in 4th-century Roman art.
The catacomb on the Via Anapo is anonymous: its ancient name is not known.
